input:
Labeled defect
- root cause: The missing or invalid CA bundle path check in cert_verify emits warnings.warn instead of raising OSError, so the failure no longer stops the request.
- failure path: A user passes verify="/etc/ssl/missing.pem" (or certifi returns an empty path); only a warning is emitted and execution continues to configure the connection with a nonexistent bundle, producing a later, misleading SSL or TypeError at connect time instead of the clear OSError.

Reviewer finding
- description: When the CA bundle path does not exist, the code now only emits a warning instead of raising OSError, and the removed extract_zipped_paths call means zipped installs now hit this path.
- rationale: Trigger: requests is loaded from a zip archive (or the bundle is otherwise missing) with verify left at its default, so DEFAULT_CA_BUNDLE_PATH points into the archive and os.path.exists returns False. The changed code only warns and continues with a nonexistent cert_loc, so the request proceeds to TLS setup with an invalid CA path. Impact: the user gets a warning and then an obscure SSL failure later, instead of the clear OSError that previously explained the missing bundle, and the zip-extraction fallback that made this work is gone.
critique: The finding names the same mechanism: when the CA bundle path doesn't exist, cert_verify warns instead of raising OSError. Execution then continues to TLS setup with an invalid path, which produces a later, obscure SSL failure. The extra point about the zip-extraction fallback is additional context and does not change the core defect.
